changes: The SYNTH page's bottom bar no longer shows 808 or 909: knob B's label already says which (TON for the 808, SWT for the 909), and the bar's right end stays free for other modules.
Takes about 5 KB less of the Rytm's module memory, so BD ANALOG fits in larger module sets.
The sound is unchanged: knob settings are stored more compactly, within a hair of the earlier values.
First release, for Analog Rytm MKII OS 1.74: BD ANALOG plays Analog BD's 808 and 909 bass drums on the BD, SD and BT tracks, through the voice's own filter, AMP and OVR.
The 909 follows Analog BD 0.1.7, refitted to a recorded TR-909.
Tap B on the SYNTH page to switch 808 and 909; the type is saved with the sound. Velocity is the accent.
Up to three BD ANALOG voices can hit at the same instant; hits spread across the beat cost less.
Ported from repeat98's Octatrack module, with his permission.
